memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then he said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak just once more. What if only ten can be found there?" He answered, "For the sake of ten, I will not destroy it." When the Lord had finished speaking with Abraham, he left, and Abraham returned home. - Gen 18:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham's final plea: "What if only ten?" And God agrees - for the sake of just ten righteous people, He would spare the entire city. The intercession ends here, but not because God ran out of mercy. Abraham stopped asking; God never stopped granting. Every single request Abraham made, God had answered yes.

Reflect on what this whole conversation reveals. God's mercy is vast - vaster than Abraham's boldest asking. Abraham went from fifty down to ten, and God said yes at every step. We are left wondering: would God have gone lower still? The limit was never God's willingness to show mercy; it was Abraham's willingness to keep asking.

This is a searching thought for our own prayers. How often do we stop asking long before God stops giving? We set the limits on God's generosity by our own small faith, our own quickness to give up. But God's mercy runs deeper than our deepest request.

And here is the wonder the whole scene points to: in the end, Sodom did not even have ten righteous people. Human righteousness could not save it. But God found a way to rescue the one righteous man in it, Lot (as the next chapter shows) - and ultimately, God provided the one truly Righteous One, Jesus, whose single righteousness saves a countless multitude. God's mercy is beyond measure. Never stop asking for it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you stop asking long before God stops giving?
- Have you underestimated the vastness of God's mercy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, Your mercy is beyond measure, deeper than my boldest asking. Forgive me for limiting Your generosity by my small faith. Thank You that in Christ, the one Righteous One, You have provided salvation beyond measure.
Amen.
